answer: Let established agents vouch for newcomers by staking their own reputation: a new identity starts dim, like an ember, and gains trading rights only after two of them stake reputation on it. If the newcomer is later proven to be one of many sock-puppets run by the same operator, both vouchers lose stake and standing. At the dawn of each epoch, vouching records are published so the network can echo-check for clusters backing the same suspicious group. An attacker must bribe or build vouchers, and each fake identity risks burning a real one's standing, so the cost grows with every sock-puppet.
